677	Preparing and ending a Round
678	A game alternates Day and Night Rounds. The scenario sets how many.
679	At the start of each Round after the first: flip the Day/Night board, reroll all the Source dice (at least half in basic colours, otherwise reroll the gold and black dice) and lay out a new Units Offer (number of players + 2).
680	The Spell and Advanced Action Offers slide: the bottom card goes back under its deck, a new one arrives at the top.
681	Each player reshuffles all their cards, Wounds included, then draws up to their Hand Limit. Their Spent Units become Ready again, as do their flipped Skills. Wounded Units stay Wounded.
682	Each player chooses a Tactic card, the player with the least Fame first. The Tactic's number sets the Turn Order: the lowest number goes first.
683	If your Deck is empty at the start of your turn, you may announce the end of the Round instead of playing. Each other player then plays one last turn. Empty deck and empty hand: you must announce it.
684	At the start of your turn, your Deck is empty but you still have 3 cards in hand.
685	You must announce the end of the Round
686	You choose: announce the end of the Round or play a turn
687	You reshuffle your discard pile to draw
688	Announcing is only mandatory if your hand is empty too. You never reshuffle your discard pile during a Round.

690	The player with the most Fame
691	The player with the least Fame
692	The first player in the previous Turn Order
693	The player lowest on the Fame track chooses first. If tied, the one whose Turn Order token is lowest.
694	You announce the end of the Round. What happens?
695	You play your turn, then the Round stops
696	You don't play; each other player plays one last turn
697	The Round stops immediately for everyone
698	The announcement replaces your turn. You don't even benefit from a Mine or a Glade.
699	The turn
700	The turn in detail
701	Regular Turn: an optional Movement, then a single action (combat, interaction, entering an adventure site). No more Movement after the action.
702	Rest, instead: no Movement and no action. Standard Rest: discard one non-Wound card and as many Wounds as you like. Slow Recovery, if you only have Wounds: show your hand and discard just one.
703	Special effects and Healing can be played at any time during your turn, even during a Rest. Only exception: no Healing during a combat.
704	Every turn, you must play or discard at least one card.
705	A card played for one effect can't then be used for its other effect.
706	You can take back your choices as long as nothing new has been revealed: tile, Enemy token, drawn card, rolled die.
707	End of turn, in order: reroll used dice, any forced Withdrawal, return Mana tokens and discard played cards, Mine or Glade effect, combat rewards, Level change, free discard (never Wounds), draw up to your Limit.
708	You Rest. What can you still do this turn?
709	Move one space
710	Play a Healing card
711	Recruit at the Village you are in
712	Resting forbids Movement, combat and interaction. Healing and special effects are still allowed, before or after.
713	Your hand holds 4 Wounds and nothing else. You Rest. How many do you discard?
714	All 4
715	Just one
717	It is a Slow Recovery: a single Wound goes to the discard pile.
718	In the middle of a combat, you gain enough Fame to cross a line. When do you change Level?
719	Right away
720	At the end of the turn, before drawing
721	At the start of the next Round
722	Level changes are always resolved at the end of the turn.
723	Movement and exploration, the details
724	Revealing a tile costs 2 points from a space adjacent to its position. Its position and orientation are fixed, and nothing is placed beyond the coastline.
725	You freely alternate moving and exploring, and you can play new cards along the way.
726	Entering an unconquered fortified site stops your Movement and starts the assault. A rampaging enemy's space is off-limits until it is defeated.
727	An adventure site can always be ignored: you pass through or stop without fighting.
728	You can pass through another player's space without stopping. Stopping there means attacking them.
729	Several effects reducing a terrain cost add up, never going below 0.
730	Forced Withdrawal: if you end your turn on an unsafe space (normally inaccessible terrain, unconquered fortified site, another Hero's space), you move back space by space and take one Wound per space.
731	Entering a City always costs 2, whatever its terrain.
732	A Dungeon is on your path. Can you cross its space without fighting there?
733	Yes, an adventure site can be ignored
734	No, entering it triggers the combat
735	Yes, but paying 2 more points
736	Only unconquered fortified sites and rampaging enemies block or interrupt Movement.
737	Thanks to an effect, you end your turn on a Lake and must move back 2 spaces to find a safe space.
738	Nothing else happens
739	You take 2 Wounds
740	You lose 2 Reputation
741	Forced Withdrawal costs one Wound per space moved back.
742	Day and Night
743	What Night changes
744	Terrain: Forest costs 5 instead of 3, Desert 3 instead of 5.
745	Gold mana can't be used at Night, wherever it comes from. Black mana can't be used by Day.
746	Black isn't a wildcard: at Night, it is mainly used for the stronger effect of Spells.
747	By Day, the garrison of a Keep or a Mage Tower is revealed as soon as a player arrives on an adjacent space. At Night, it stays hidden until the assault.
748	A Ruins token placed at Night stays face down until a player enters the space, or until the next Day.
749	In a Dungeon, Night rules apply even in broad Day.
750	Crystals: a Crystal turns back into pure mana whenever you like; the reverse requires an effect. Three per colour at most: an extra Crystal gained from an effect becomes a simple Mana token, one from a Mine or a reward is lost.
751	It is Night. A card gave you a gold mana token. Can it pay for the stronger effect of a green card?
752	Yes, gold replaces any colour
753	No, gold can't be used at Night
754	Yes, but only if it comes from a card
755	At Night, gold mana is useless, wherever it comes from.
756	At Night, you stop next to a Keep whose token is face down.
757	The token is revealed
758	It stays hidden, unless you assault
759	It is revealed then hidden again
760	Revealing by simple proximity only works by Day.
761	How much does entering a Desert cost during a Night Round?
762	Desert costs 5 by Day and 3 at Night. Forest does the opposite.
764	Learning and casting Spells
765	A Spell is a player card: it joins your Deck and is drawn like the others.
766	Even its basic effect costs one mana of its colour.
767	Stronger effect: one mana of its colour and one black mana. So it is only possible at Night, or in a Dungeon.
768	You only take one die from the Source per turn: if it is the black one, the other mana must come from a Crystal, a token or an effect.
769	Like any card, a Spell can be played sideways for 1 point.
770	Buying a Spell: at a conquered Mage Tower, for 7 Influence plus one mana of the Spell's colour. You can also gain them as rewards. It goes on top of your Deck, and the Offer is refilled from the top.
771	By Day, what must you pay for the basic effect of a red Spell?
772	Nothing, like an Action card
773	A red mana
774	A red mana and a black mana
775	A Spell always requires one mana of its colour, even for its basic effect. Gold also works by Day.
776	At Night, with no Crystal or token. The Source shows a black die and a blue die. Can you cast the stronger effect of a blue Spell?
777	Yes, by taking both dice
778	No: only one Source die per turn
779	Yes, the black is enough
780	You need two manas and the Source only provides one per turn, unless an effect gives more.
781	At a conquered Mage Tower, learning a green Spell costs…
782	7 Influence
783	7 Influence and a green mana
784	6 Influence
785	7 Influence and one mana of the Spell's colour. Six points is the price of an Advanced Action at the Monastery.
787	Artifacts and Banners
788	Basic effect: the Artifact is played like a normal card, then goes to the discard pile.
789	Stronger effect: instead of paying mana, you destroy the Artifact. It is removed from the game.
790	It can also be played sideways for 1 point.
791	Artifacts are gained at the end of the turn: draw as many as you gained, plus one. Put one back under the deck, the others go on top of your Deck. There is never an Artifact Offer.
792	Banner: an Artifact you attach to a Unit, at any time during your turn. The Unit benefits from its basic effect. Only one Banner per Unit, and no stronger effect while it is attached.
793	If the Unit is destroyed or disbanded, the Banner goes to the discard pile. At the end of the Round, you leave it on the Unit or shuffle it into your Deck.
794	You gain an Artifact. How many cards do you draw from the Artifact deck?
796	Two, and you keep one
797	Three, and you keep one
798	Always one more than the number gained, to leave a choice.
799	You use an Artifact's stronger effect. Where does the card go?
800	To your discard pile
801	It is removed from the game
802	Under the Artifact deck
803	The stronger effect destroys the Artifact.
804	You disband a Unit carrying a Banner. The Banner…
805	is removed from the game with the Unit
806	goes to your discard pile
807	returns to your hand
808	You will draw it again later, often in a following Round.
810	Levels and Skills
811	You gain a Level for each line crossed on the Fame track, at the end of the turn. The maximum is Level 10.
812	Odd level: the next Level token becomes visible (Armor or Hand Limit goes up) and you receive one more Command token.
813	Even level: a Skill and an Advanced Action. Reveal two tiles from your stack, keep one, place the other in the common Offer, then take the Advanced Action of your choice from the Offer.
814	Even-level variant: instead, take a Skill left by another player in the common Offer. Your two tiles go there, and you receive the Advanced Action from the bottom of the Offer.
815	Three kinds of Skills: usable once per turn; once per Round (the tile is flipped); interactive, once per Round, whose effect lasts until your next turn and affects the other players.
816	Any newly gained card goes on top of your Deck.
817	You reach Level 3. What do you gain?
818	A Skill and an Advanced Action
819	A Command token and the next Level token
820	A Spell
821	Odd Levels improve Armor or Hand Limit and add a Command token.
822	Level 4: you prefer the Skill another player left in the common Offer. Which Advanced Action do you receive?
823	The one of your choice
824	The one at the bottom of the Offer
825	Taking someone else's Skill deprives you of the card choice.
826	Units in detail
827	Two decks: Regular Units (silver back) and Elite Units (gold back). As soon as a Core tile is revealed, the Offer alternates Elite and Regular.
828	A Unit can only be recruited at a site whose icon appears on its card, for its Influence cost. The Units Offer is only refilled at the next Round.
829	With no free Command token, you must disband a Unit to recruit another. The recruit arrives Ready and can be used right away, but not to pay for its own recruitment.
830	Activating a Unit makes it Spent until the end of the Round. Some abilities also require a mana.
831	A Spent Unit can still absorb Damage. A Wounded Unit can neither act nor absorb.
832	Healing a Unit costs as many Healing points as its level, for each Wound.
833	Unit Resistant to the attack's type: it first absorbs its Armor without being Wounded. If Damage remains, it is Wounded and absorbs its Armor a second time. In any case, it only absorbs once per combat.
834	A Unit with Armor 4 and Physical Resistance absorbs a physical attack of 7.
835	It isn't Wounded
836	It is Wounded and everything is absorbed
837	It is Wounded and 3 Damage remain
838	4 absorbed without a Wound, then it is Wounded and absorbs the remaining 3.
839	The same Unit absorbs a physical attack of 4.
840	Nothing happens: everything is absorbed without a Wound
841	It is Wounded
842	It is destroyed
843	The Armor is enough. However, it can't absorb any more during this combat.
844	Healing a level 3 Unit with one Wound costs…
845	1 Healing point
846	3 Healing points
847	3 Influence points
848	As many Healing points as the Unit's level.
849	Elements
850	Fire, Ice and Resistances
851	Attacks and Blocks come in four types: physical, Fire, Ice and Cold Fire.
852	Blocking: against a physical attack, any Block is efficient. Against Fire, only Ice and Cold Fire. Against Ice, only Fire and Cold Fire. Against Cold Fire, only Cold Fire.
853	Inefficient Blocks are added up then halved, rounded down.
854	Enemy Resistance: your Attacks of that type are added up then halved, rounded down. Cold Fire is only reduced by an enemy resistant to both Fire and Ice.
855	A sideways card always gives one physical point, and never Ranged or Siege Attack.
856	An enemy resistant to Fire also ignores special effects, other than Attack and Block, of red cards and of Unit abilities paid with red mana. Same for Ice with blue.
857	A card's colour doesn't make the element: Attack 4" on a red card is still physical.
An enemy makes an Ice Attack 5. You play Fire Block 3 and physical Block 4. Is it blocked?
No: 1 is missing
Fire counts in full, physical for half: 3 + 2 = 5, just enough.
Enemy with Armor 4, Physical and Ice Resistance. You have Fire Attack 2 and physical Attack 5.
Defeated: 2 + 2 = 4
Insufficient: 3
Defeated: 7
Fire isn't reduced. Physical is halved, rounded down: 2.
Abilities
Enemy abilities
Fortified: during the Ranged and Siege phase, only Siege hits it. Defenders of a fortified site are always Fortified. A Fortified enemy defending a fortified site is untouchable in this phase.
Swift: its Attack is doubled, but only for Blocking.
Brutal: its Attack is doubled, but only for Damage.
Poison: each Wound taken into your hand adds another to your discard pile. A Unit Wounded by it receives two Wounds.
Paralyze: if your Hero takes its Damage, you discard all your non-Wound cards. A Unit that would be Wounded is destroyed.
Summon: in the Block phase, draw a brown token. It attacks instead of the summoner, then is discarded. Blocking it earns no Fame.
Knocked out: if in one combat you take as many Wounds as your unmodified Hand Limit, you discard all your other cards. Units and Skills remain usable.
An enemy with Attack 3 is Swift and Brutal. How much Block do you need, and how much Damage if it gets through?
Block 6, Damage 6
Block 6, Damage 3
Block 3, Damage 6
Swift doubles the Attack for Blocking, Brutal doubles it for Damage.
A Poison enemy deals 2 Wounds to your Hero. Result?
2 Wounds in hand
2 in hand and 2 in the discard pile
4 in hand
Each Wound taken into your hand comes with a Wound placed in the discard pile.
A Keep's garrison has the Fortified ability. You have Siege Attack 6 in the first phase.
It is defeated if its Armor is 6 or less
Impossible: doubly Fortified, it is untouchable in this phase
Siege is halved
You'll have to wait for the Attack phase, where fortifications no longer count.
Several enemies
Fighting several enemies
One combat per turn, but it can include several enemies: a site with several tokens, rampaging enemies provoked by your Movement, adjacent rampaging enemies you challenge as well.
When entering an adventure site, you can't challenge anyone else. And never enemies and a player in the same combat.
Attacking: target one or more enemies and match the sum of their Armors. You can make several separate attacks in the same phase.
In a targeted group, a single Resistance reduces all your Attacks of that type, and a single Fortified forbids Ranged Attacks in the first phase. Splitting your attacks avoids these penalties.
Blocking: one enemy at a time, never a group Block.
Damage: each enemy neither defeated nor blocked strikes, in the order you choose.
During an assault, rampaging enemies joining in aren't Fortified, and you don't need to defeat them to conquer the site.
Two enemies: Armor 3 with Physical Resistance, and Armor 4 with no Resistance. You make a single physical Attack of 7 against both.
Both are defeated
Neither: the attack drops to 3 against 7 Armor
Only the second is defeated
One enemy's Resistance reduces the whole group attack. Targeting only the second, 7 was more than enough.
Two unblocked enemies, with Attack 3 and 4. Can you play a single Block of 7 against the group?
Yes, their Attacks add up
No, each enemy is blocked separately
Yes, but only if they are the same type
Each Block targets a single enemy. Here you need a Block of 3 and another of 4.
